newsitem.title: UK: FOMC leaves T-bonds cold,BTPs best bet technically.
newsitem.headline: FOMC leaves T-bonds cold,BTPs best bet technically.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady was an anti-climax for the technical outlook for Treasuries, analysts said on Tuesday.
The long-awaited outcome failed to jolt the market out of its three week stupor of consolidation and technical indicators remain stuck in neutral.
"Technicals are extremely neutral, the market is trendless" said Bill Westgate, Vice-President as HSBC Securities here.
"We've got to ruminate where the next potential move could come from. My gut feeling is that it will be up, but we haven't got the technicals to support that, it's just based on fundamentals."

So with Treasuries dawdling in neutral, investors may be tempted to look to European bond markets. But some analysts say both Bunds and gilts look ripe for a downside correction, leaving BTPs the best bet for a quick return.
"But it will have to be very quick," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking here.
"The market has been in a straight forward uptrend for three weeks --so it is probably healthiest in terms of momentum, which is very good short term, but it probably does need a correction most."
He said the market had likely priced in the best part of an Italian rate cut, leaving it with the potential for a small push up to 131.80, before any sell-off.
"So short term it will outperform the best, but it is vulnerable to a correction."
By 0948 GMT, June BTPs were up 40 basis points at 131.29.
Ostwald said the recent rally in both Bunds and gilts lacked momentum, leaving them in a precarious position.
He said Bunds would stuggle to get through 101.90, but if they did, could go to 102.50, then the 103.16 contract high from February 28.
"But any setback through the 101.53 short term trendline would see a longer term correction to the whole up-cycle...to test 100.34,38," he said.

Robin Wilkin, senior technical analysts, MCM YieldWatch here was slighlty more optimistic on the technical outlook for Bunds, saying they would likely consolidate near-term, before a push up to around 102.10.
"Eventually, over the long term, it can go up towards 103.16, the contract high on February 28," he said.
By 0949 GMT, June Bunds on LIFFE were up 28 basis points at 101.90.
Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London, said at a push, the gilt market was in slightly better condition than Treasuries, technically.
"There's not a great deal in it, but on balance I think gilts look slightly healthier from a technical view," he said.
"They've advanced after the election and although daily studies are still in a correction phase, there's not enough negative price action to break the view that there is still upside potential."
One thing analysts did agree on was that Treasuries were looking tired and would only manage to consolidate near term.
They said tough resistance at the May second high of 110-10, then the May 13 high of 110-22 would cap the market.
Ostwald favoured a slide back to 108-30 before further gains could materialise.
